findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded-post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme value silently jumped from 30% to 70% lightness. Since `dark-light-choose`'s first argument is the light-theme value, the author name in expanded reply/in-reply-to blocks becomes a very washed-out grey on light themes (a visible contrast regression), whereas every other conversion in this PR keeps the light value and only adds the complementary dark value. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
findings.body: The previous value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the change produces `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the light-theme value was changed from 70% to 30%, making this hint text much darker than before on light themes and inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94 uses 70% / 30%). The two arguments look like they were swapped; it should read `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: `.topic-map h3` light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The topic-map heading was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme color is therefore 30 percentage points lighter than before, so the mobile topic-map heading loses contrast and no longer matches the desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321 keeps 20% / 80%). The intended conversion is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color lightened from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for the member name while the sibling `.title` used 50%, giving the name visually stronger emphasis. The change sets the name to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so on light themes the name is now the same washed-out grey as the title and the intended hierarchy is lost. Only the dark variant should have been added: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color lightened from 30% to 50% (mobile)
findings.body: Same regression as in the desktop stylesheet: the member name was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now resolves to 50% lightness on light themes, making it identical to the adjacent `.title` (50%) and removing the emphasis difference. The light-theme argument of `dark-light-choose` should stay at 30%, with 70% used for the dark variant.

findings.title: Stale comment referencing the old topic-list default color
findings.body: The comment "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)" no longer matches the code: `common/base/_topic-list.scss` now sets table cells with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Leaving the old expression documented here is misleading for anyone later adjusting the coldmap colors for dark schemes.
